stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a prescription for a brand-name biological product. The prescriber has not prohibited substitution. The pharmacy has a less expensive FDA-licensed biosimilar, but FDA has not determined that product to be interchangeable with the prescribed biologic. May the pharmacist substitute that biosimilar under Massachusetts' statutory biologic-substitution authority without obtaining new prescriber authorization?

choices.text: Yes, because every FDA-licensed biosimilar is automatically interchangeable for pharmacy substitution.
Yes, because the absence of a prescriber prohibition is the only condition Massachusetts imposes.
No. The statutory substitution pathway requires an FDA determination that the substitute is interchangeable with the prescribed biological product.
No, because Massachusetts prohibits pharmacist substitution of any biological product.
Yes, but only if the patient waives notification to the prescriber.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c.112, §12EE authorizes pharmacist substitution when FDA has determined the biological product is interchangeable with the prescribed brand-name biological product and the prescriber has not prohibited substitution. Biosimilar licensure alone does not satisfy the interchangeable-product condition.

choice_analysis.A: Biosimilar status does not automatically establish interchangeability for this statutory pathway.
choice_analysis.B: Absence of a prescriber prohibition is necessary but not sufficient.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: FDA interchangeability is a statutory condition for pharmacist substitution.
choice_analysis.D: Massachusetts permits substitution when the statutory conditions are met.
choice_analysis.E: Patient waiver does not replace the required interchangeability determination.

explanation.mpje_trap: Do not treat 'biosimilar' and 'interchangeable' as synonyms.

reasoning_steps: Separate FDA biosimilar licensure from an FDA interchangeability determination
Check for prescriber prohibition as a separate condition
Apply the Massachusetts substitution statute only when both the product and prescription conditions are satisfied
